title: Dataset Condensation for Time Series Classification via Dual Domain Matching

problem.claim: Managing large quantities of time series data creates challenges for deep learning tasks, particularly deep neural network training.

gap.claim: Existing dataset condensation methods are primarily designed for image and graph datasets and perform suboptimally when directly adapted to time series because they do not effectively leverage frequency-domain information.

contributions.claim: A framework named CondTSC for dataset condensation in time series classification.
A condensed dataset generation approach that matches surrogate objectives in both the time and frequency domains.
A framework incorporating multi-view data augmentation, dual-domain training, and dual surrogate objectives.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish CondTSC from previous methods by matching surrogate objectives across both time and frequency domains.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments reportedly show that CondTSC outperforms other baselines.
The learned condensed synthetic dataset reportedly exhibits desirable characteristics, including conformity to the original data distribution.

narrative_sequence.summary: Time series data is important across research fields.
Large-scale time series data is difficult to manage for deep learning, motivating dataset condensation.
Existing condensation methods do not adequately exploit time-series information, especially in the frequency domain.
CondTSC performs dual-domain matching using augmentation, dual-domain training, and dual surrogate objectives.
The authors report improved baseline performance and desirable distributional characteristics in the condensed dataset.

source_observation.claim: Matching surrogate objectives in both time and frequency domains is used to address information loss from applying image- or graph-oriented condensation methods to time series.

interpretation.claim: For structured sequential data, condensation objectives may need to represent complementary domains rather than relying on a single representation.

application.claim: Use complementary time- and frequency-domain objectives when designing condensed datasets for time series classification.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether dual-domain matching is necessary for every time series dataset or task.

unknowns: Dataset sizes, datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are not specified.
The abstract does not describe the optimization procedure, model architecture, or computational cost.
Generalization beyond time series classification is not established.
